% ====================================================================== section 0
\section{Summary: three lists and three decisions}\label{sec:ark-summary}

\textbf{What was examined.} For nine generic components of the proof system (the sumcheck;
batching; fingerprints, the grand product, GKR and stacking; composition and the framework
question; oracle interfaces; Fiat--Shamir and BCS; WHIR, FRI, Basefold and the coding theory;
ring switching; the typed \code{Interaction} framework), what ArkLib implements at the old pin
\code{dca90385} and the new pin \code{7653a901}, what landed since (nothing: \code{origin/main}
is the new pin), what its open pull requests would supply, and what leanerVM must build itself.
Sources: the two revisions read with \code{git show}, both axiom baselines, every relevant open
and merged pull request and issue read with \code{gh}, the blueprint and status at
\code{b435631}, and four sibling dossiers.

\subsection{Implemented and usable at the new pin (with the adaptor it needs)}\label{sec:ark-list-usable}

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
\item The typed one-polynomial sumcheck (pull requests \#872--\#892, \#1214, \#1216, \#1235,
  \#1242, \#1243): a computable verifier and honest prover on CompPoly data, perfect
  completeness, and \emph{plain} soundness \code{count·deg/|F|} against every native prover ---
  no round-by-round notion, no extractor, \code{Unit} witness, on the typed framework; consumable
  for the plain case through an \code{OracleReduction}-to-native correspondence lemma that nobody
  has written (\cref{sec:ark-sumcheck}).
\item The typed framework's plain composition soundness (\#1218, \#1231--\#1238), not consumable
  by the spine (no knowledge notion; \cref{sec:ark-typed}).
\item Schwartz--Zippel restated on VCVio's sampler (\lean{prob_eval_zero_le_div},
  \lean{prob_eval_zero_univ_le_div}), consumable directly (\cref{f:ark-schwartz-zippel}).
\item A \emph{proved} Johnson-range affine-line mutual-correlated-agreement bound over any finite
  field (\lean{ReedSolomon.mcaError_affineLine_johnson_le}, from the completed \#907 port), with
  a constant different from the admitted [BCHKS25] one Annex B cites; consumable if its constant
  meets the parameters (unverified; \cref{sec:ark-whir}).
\item The pairwise Johnson list bound (\#910), interleaving and folding lemmas (building blocks,
  fit unverified).
\item In VCVio at \code{a4232d08}: Merkle trees with proved completeness and single-opening
  random-oracle extractability (ArkLib issue \#4 closed, moved to VCVio \#571;
  \cref{sec:ark-fs}).
\item The ring-switching packing profile structure with its coordinates repaired (\#896); its
  protocol's security leaves all admitted (\cref{sec:ark-ring}).
\end{enumerate}

State and dates as read on 2026-09-30.
\begin{itemize}

  mergeable, unreviewed).

\subsection{Ours to build}\label{sec:ark-list-ours}

\begin{itemize}
\item The four leanVM sumcheck shapes (virtual summand with the final table-value message;
  eq-weighted back-loaded over tables of different heights; the normalized Gruen round of the
  GKR; the dropped-coefficient encoding) with their round-by-round knowledge leaves.
\item The batching component (the opening phase under the inner-product interface).
\item The fingerprint, product lemma and collision bound.
\item The radix-4 GKR with its binary first layer.
\item The inner-product oracle interface.
\item WHIR over binary Reed--Solomon codes with grinding.
\item The Merkle/BLAKE2s instantiation over VCVio's trees; the BLAKE2s chain as a challenge
  oracle, the grinding checks, the proof object.
\item The three compiled-security interfaces stated for leanVM's construction, and the
  list-binding compilation.
\item The $\mathrm{GF}(2) \to \K$ ring-switching profile and Annex A's protocol (leanerVM issue
  \#3).
\item The plain-knowledge corollary in the stateless form.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The decisions the owner must take}\label{sec:ark-decisions}

\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
\item \textbf{Framework.} Stay on \code{OracleReduction} (the only framework with knowledge
  soundness) and own the composition (done), or migrate now and wait for notions that do not
  exist (\cref{sec:ark-composition,sec:ark-typed}). \emph{Recommendation:} stay on
  \code{OracleReduction} and keep owning the composition; write a ledger row saying so and
  naming ArkLib's roadmap items 3--4 as the trigger to revisit.
\item \textbf{Sumcheck.} Consume the typed sumcheck through an adaptor for the \emph{plain}
  one-polynomial case (honest prover, computable verifier, plain soundness) and write the four
  leanVM variants locally with their round-by-round knowledge leaves; or keep the whole of
  Layer 4 local. Either way the leaf proofs are ours; the adaptor buys the computable honest
  prover and the algebra of \#1128 and leanerVM \#42, and costs a correspondence lemma between
  an \code{OracleReduction} run and the native \code{execute}. \emph{Recommendation:} consume
  the typed sumcheck only for the plain one-polynomial case through an adaptor, and write the
  leanVM variants and every knowledge leaf locally; drop the plan to ``contribute the leaf''
  upstream (the leaf is false as stated until \#1244, and upstream's direction is the typed
  framework).
\item \textbf{The inner-product oracle.} Not an upstream question: nothing upstream has it or
  plans it. \emph{Recommendation:} define it locally; the spine should define it
  (gt-opening-compile A.5 (ii); \cref{sec:ark-oracles}).
\end{enumerate}

\subsection{Findings by severity}\label{sec:ark-findings-summary}

\begin{itemize}
\item \sev{major} The classical sumcheck leaf the ledger targets is false as stated at both pins
  (\cref{f:ark-sumcheck-leaf-false}); the holes for the virtual sumcheck and for its
  round-by-round knowledge soundness (G1, G2) name upstream sources of the wrong kind
  (\cref{f:ark-sumcheck-holes-sources}); the ledger row on mutual correlated agreement up to
  Johnson (A8) and the status's coding-theory row are stale in both directions --- the watched
  port is complete without proving the cited theorem, a proved substitute exists, and the
  capacity results exclude characteristic two (\cref{f:ark-mca-stale}).
\item \sev{minor} The hole for Merkle trees, BLAKE2s bytes and the WHIR parameters (K2) cites a
  closed issue and misses VCVio's proved Merkle library (\cref{f:ark-merkle-closed-issue}); the
  batching source is a lemma in a pull request that will not merge as is
  (\cref{f:ark-batching-source}); the deletion condition of the port and the plain corollary
  should be restated on \#1245's evidence (\cref{f:ark-port-deletion}); the status's upstream
  watch is out of date on eight rows (\cref{f:ark-status-watch}).
\item \sev{note} The Schwartz--Zippel citation (\cref{f:ark-schwartz-zippel}).
\end{itemize}
No finding contradicts the brief; the brief's §7 fact that the generic components are
``specified in the blueprint and not built'' stands, with the qualification that a plain
one-polynomial sumcheck is now built upstream.

% ====================================================================== section 2
\section{The sumcheck}\label{sec:ark-sumcheck}

\paragraph{(a) At the old pin \texttt{dca90385}.}
\file{ArkLib/ProofSystem/Sumcheck/} had seven files: \file{Domain.lean},
\file{Impl/Basic.lean}, \file{Spec/General.lean}, \file{Spec/SingleRound.lean},
\file{Structured.lean}, \file{Structured/Prismalinear.lean}, \file{Structured/SingleRound.lean}.
\file{ArkLib/Interaction/} had seven files (the typed core) and no sumcheck on it.

\emph{The classical specification} (\file{Spec/}), stated on the legacy \code{OracleReduction}
framework:
\begin{itemize}
\item \lean{Sumcheck.Spec.StatementRound R n i} (\file{Spec/SingleRound.lean:130-133} at both
  pins): a target and the challenges so far.
  \lean{Sumcheck.Spec.OracleStatement R n deg := fun _ : Unit ↦ R⦃≤ deg⦄[X Fin n]} (\code{:141}),
  one Mathlib multivariate polynomial of individual degree at most \code{deg} with the
  evaluation oracle interface. \lean{relationRound} (\code{:144-147}): the running sum over the
  domain \code{D : Fin m ↪ R} equals the target.
\item The single round
  \lean{Sumcheck.Spec.SingleRound.Simple.{prover,verifier,oracleVerifier,reduction,oracleReduction}}
  (\code{:365-448}), the round-$i$ versions obtained by context lifting (\code{:800-830}), and the
  full protocol \lean{Sumcheck.Spec.{pSpec,verifier,oracleVerifier,reduction,oracleReduction}}
  (\file{Spec/General.lean:129-195}) as \code{seqCompose} of the rounds.
\item Theorems: \lean{Sumcheck.Spec.SingleRound.Simple.reduction_perfectCompleteness}
  (\code{:531}, proved in the file, no \code{sorry}), \lean{Simple.verifier_rbrKnowledgeSoundness}
  and \lean{Simple.oracleVerifier_rbrKnowledgeSoundness} (\code{:570-579}, both \code{sorry}),
  \lean{Sumcheck.Spec.reduction_perfectCompleteness} (\file{General.lean:211}, proved from
  \lean{seqCompose_perfectCompleteness_of_guarded_verifiers} and the single-round completeness,
  but its round-$i$ leaf \lean{SingleRound.reduction_perfectCompleteness} goes through the
  admitted \lean{Reduction.liftContext_perfectCompleteness}, so the baseline lists it),
  \lean{Sumcheck.Spec.oracleVerifier_rbrKnowledgeSoundness} (\file{General.lean:223}, from the
  admitted \lean{OracleVerifier.seqCompose_rbrKnowledgeSoundness} and the admitted leaf; in the
  baseline).
\end{itemize}

\emph{A defect of the legacy verifier, found upstream after the pin.} The
\lean{Simple.verifier} computes its next target from the \emph{input} polynomial, not the sent
one:
\src{\file{ArkLib/ProofSystem/Sumcheck/Spec/SingleRound.lean:391-397} (\code{7653a901}; identical at \code{dca90385})}
\begin{leancode}
def verifier : Verifier oSpec (StmtIn R × (∀ i, OStmtIn R deg i))
    (StmtOut R × (∀ i, OStmtOut R deg i)) (pSpec R deg) where
  verify := fun ⟨target, oStmt⟩ transcript => do
    letI polyLE := transcript 0
    guard (∑ x ∈ (univ.map D), polyLE.val.eval x = target)
    letI chal := transcript 1
    pure ⟨⟨(oStmt ()).val.eval chal, chal⟩, fun _ => oStmt ()⟩
\end{leancode}
and \lean{Simple.oracleVerifier} (\code{:423-436}) queries \code{[OStmtIn R deg]ₒ} at the
challenge for \code{newTarget}. Issue \#1, comment of 2026-09-27 (quangvdao, ``source inspection
at \code{c8f2353d3}, independently confirmed''): ``\lean{Sumcheck.Spec.SingleRound.Simple.verifier}
checks the prover message's sum but sets \code{newTarget} to the original input polynomial's
evaluation at the challenge. \ldots{} Consequently, over $\F_5$, with degree bound zero, domain
$\{0\}$, input polynomial $p = 0$, claimed sum $s = 1$, and prover message $q = 1$, the input
relation is false and the sum check passes.'' Since the output statement \code{(p(r), r)} always
satisfies \code{outputRelation} (\code{:354}: \code{(oStmt ()).1.eval chal = newTarget}), a false
input claim is turned into an accepted, true output claim with probability one, and the admitted
\lean{Simple.verifier_rbrKnowledgeSoundness} at error \code{deg/|R| = 0} cannot hold (paper
reasoning of the survey; the upstream comment and the regression test of \#1244,
\file{ArkLibTest/ProofSystem/Sumcheck/LegacyVerifier.lean}, ``the sum check passes, but the
output relation remains false for every challenge'', establish the defect). Pull request \#1244
(open, 2026-09-27, mergeable, no review) changes the line to \code{polyLE.val.eval chal} and the
oracle verifier to query \code{[(pSpec R deg).Message]ₒ}. The round-$i$ verifier (\code{:800})
is \lean{Simple.verifier} under \code{liftContext} (\#1244's \lean{verifier_eq_unfolded} unfolds
exactly that), so the whole classical protocol inherits the defect at both pins
(\cref{f:ark-sumcheck-leaf-false}).

\emph{The structured (witness-mode) sumcheck} (\file{Structured.lean},
\file{Structured/Prismalinear.lean}, \file{Structured/SingleRound.lean}; no \code{sorry}) is the
degree-2 $H = m \cdot t$ sumcheck of Binius Basefold and ring switching, where $t$ is a committed
multilinear and $m$ a context-dependent multilinear multiplier (\file{Structured.lean:11-25}). It
supplies round-polynomial computation and degree bookkeeping (\lean{computeRoundPoly},
\lean{projectToNextSumcheckPoly}, \lean{getSumcheckRoundPoly}, \lean{roundOracleReduction},
\code{roundKnowledgeError := d/|L|} as a definition) and \textbf{no security theorem} in these
files; its docstring says ``the two modes carry independent proofs'' and the refinement to the
canonical mode ``is left for follow-up work''.

\paragraph{(b) At the new pin \texttt{7653a901}.}
The classical \file{Spec/} is unchanged except for the \code{Simple} leaves' proof bodies
(\file{Spec/SingleRound.lean}: 211 lines changed, no statement changed; 14 lines still contain
\code{sorry}) and \file{Domain.lean} (3 lines). What is new is \textbf{the typed (``native'')
sumcheck}, 22 files under \file{Sumcheck/Interaction/} and two under \file{Impl/}, built between
2026-09-12 (\#872) and 2026-09-27 (\#1243). It is stated on the typed \code{Interaction}
framework, not on \code{OracleReduction}. The objects, from scratch:
\begin{itemize}
\item An \lean{Interaction.Oracle.Protocol} is a typed tree of moves;
  \code{.oracleWith M interface rest} is ``the prover sends a message of type \code{M} readable
  only through \code{interface : OracleInterface M}, then \code{rest}''; \code{.public .receiver T k}
  is ``the verifier sends a public value of type \code{T}, then \code{k value}''. A
  \lean{Prover.Strategy} / \lean{Verifier.Strategy} is a monadic program over such a tree.
  \lean{VirtualOracle} (\file{Interaction/Oracle/Virtual.lean}) implements an oracle by a program
  over earlier oracles; a \lean{ClosedClaim} (\file{Oracle/Claim.lean}) is a statement plus the
  \emph{observable answers} of its oracles, so relations see answers, never representations.
\item The protocol (\file{Sumcheck/Interaction/Protocol.lean:41-46}): for \code{count} rounds, the
  prover sends a \code{Message} (a univariate polynomial of degree at most \code{deg},
  \file{SingleRound.lean:32} \code{abbrev Message := R⦃≤ deg⦄[X]}, read through evaluation
  queries), then the verifier sends \code{Option R}: \code{none} is a public abort, \code{some r}
  the challenge.
\item The verifier (\file{Protocol.lean:98-121}): sums the \emph{sent} polynomial over the
  declared domain list, compares with the target, samples \code{r}, queries the sent polynomial at
  \code{r} for the next target; at the end it exports the original oracle and the claim
  \code{(target, challenges)}. The output relation (\code{:137-138}):
  \code{claim.oracles ⟨(), claim.stmt.challenges⟩ = claim.stmt.target}, ``a relation on the
  output, not a final verifier query''.
\item \textbf{Soundness} (\file{ProtocolSoundness.lean:201-215}, quoted in full):
\end{itemize}
\src{\file{ArkLib/ProofSystem/Sumcheck/Interaction/ProtocolSoundness.lean:201-215} (\code{7653a901})}
\begin{leancode}
theorem execute_soundness {m : ℕ} (D : Fin m ↪ F)
    (count start : ℕ) (finish : start + count = n) (A : PFunctor)
    (originalOracle : VirtualOracle (OracleSpec.ofPFunctor A) (polynomialFamily F n deg))
    (stmt : Spec.StatementRound F n ⟨start, by omega⟩)
    (impl : QueryImpl (OracleSpec.ofPFunctor A) Id)
    (prover : Prover.Strategy unifSpec (protocol F deg count).tree
      (protocol F deg count).roles (fun _ => Unit)) (p : Spec.OracleStatement F n deg ())
    (horiginal : originalOracle.eval impl =
      (polynomialFamily F n deg).behaviorOfRealizations (fun _ => p))
    (hfalse : ¬ closedRelation F n deg D ⟨start, by omega⟩ ⟨stmt, originalOracle.eval impl⟩) :
    Pr{let result ← (execute F n deg unifSpec ($ᵗ F) (Finset.univ.map D).toList
      count start finish A originalOracle stmt impl prover)}[
        result.map (outputRelation F n deg) = some True] ≤
      (count : ENNReal) * deg / Fintype.card F := by
\end{leancode}
\begin{itemize}
\item[] In words: for any finite domain \code{D}, any polynomial \code{p} of individual degree at
  most \code{deg} realizing the original oracle, any false running claim, and \textbf{any} native
  prover strategy (adaptive, with private memory and effects after each challenge), the
  probability that the run is not rejected and ends in a true evaluation claim is at most
  \code{count · deg / |F|}, for uniform challenges. This is \textbf{plain soundness} (a bound on
  the whole run), not round-by-round, and it is stated for an oracle that \emph{is} a polynomial:
  the witness is \code{Unit}, there is no extractor and no knowledge notion.
\item \textbf{Completeness} (\file{ProtocolCompleteness.lean:36-49, 110-126}):
  \lean{Native.honestProver} sends the projected round polynomial
  \lean{Spec.SingleRound.projectedRoundPolynomial}; \lean{execute_perfectCompleteness} gives
  probability one for any \code{ProbComp} challenge program from a true claim.
\item \textbf{The computable layer} (\#1242, \#1243): \file{Impl/Representation.lean:25}
  \code{Message := {p : CompPoly.CPolynomial R // p.degree ≤ deg}} with Horner evaluation
  (\code{:28}); \lean{Computable.protocol/verifier/execute} are the same \lean{Native.Core}
  definitions specialized (\file{Computable.lean:34-42}); \lean{Computable.execute_eq_native}
  (\code{:54}), \lean{Computable.execute_soundness} (\file{ComputableSoundness.lean:31-47}, same
  bound, \code{[BEq F] [LawfulBEq F]} added); \file{Impl/Projection.lean:187}
  \lean{projectedMessage} computes the honest message from a \code{CMvPolynomial (n+1) R} by
  CompPoly's variable split and finite sums (\#1243: ``a general finite-enumeration prover. It
  does not claim a linear-time or streaming multilinear algorithm'');
  \lean{Computable.honestProver} and \lean{Computable.execute_perfectCompleteness}
  (\file{ComputableCompleteness.lean:37, 116}).
\item \textbf{The bridge to the legacy relations} (\file{Legacy.lean}, \#874):
  \lean{legacy_input_iff} (\code{:42}), \lean{legacy_output_iff} (\code{:34}), and
  \lean{legacy_honest_verifier_correspondence} (\code{:108}), which is ``deliberately
  honest-only. The legacy verifier reads the input polynomial for its next target, while the
  typed verifier reads the actually sent polynomial'' (\#874's description) --- the defect above,
  seen from the typed side.
\item Composition (\file{Composition.lean}, \#1235): \lean{execute_eq_appendExported}
  (\code{:337}) identifies the native execution with ``first round, then the remaining rounds''
  through the typed framework's \lean{Verifier.appendExported}, and the soundness proof now goes
  through the generic \lean{executeStrategies_appendExported_soundness_ae}
  (\file{Interaction/Oracle/CompositionSoundness.lean:302}).
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{(c) On \texttt{origin/main} beyond the new pin.}
Nothing: \code{origin/main} is \code{7653a901}.

\textbf{No open pull request supplies} round-by-round or knowledge soundness of the typed
sumcheck, a virtual (formula-of-tables) summand, an eq-weighted or back-loaded variant, a
normalized (Gruen) round, or a dropped-coefficient encoding. ArkLib's roadmap
(\file{docs/design/05-roadmap.md} at \code{7653a901}, ``Complete native Sumcheck first'', items
3--5) lists as \emph{active}: ``Native round-by-round security. Define the security condition on
actual execution prefixes, instantiate it with Sumcheck's proved per-challenge bound\ldots'';
``Knowledge and extraction. Define native knowledge and round-by-round knowledge games with
explicit extractor access and timing. Current oracle Sumcheck has a \code{Unit}
witness\ldots''; ``Efficient implementations and legacy migration. Optimize the Boolean
multilinear case using CompPoly evaluation tables\ldots''. No pull request for any of the three
existed on 2026-09-30.

\paragraph{(e) What the blueprint plans locally that exists upstream.}
The blueprint's Layer 4 (\code{bp:869-904}) plans \lean{Virtual},
\code{sumcheck : OracleReduction []ₒ …}, \lean{sumcheck_perfectCompleteness},
\code{sumcheck_rbrKnowledgeSoundness … (fun _ ↦ d/|F|)}; its ledger row on the sumcheck's
round-by-round knowledge soundness (A1, \code{bp:258}) says ``Layer 4 proves the single-round
bound for its own sumcheck shape and contributes it as the missing leaf''; the hole for the
virtual sumcheck (G1) names in its ``Existing work'' column ``ArkLib \code{main}'s
\code{Sumcheck/Interaction/}'' and the hole for the sumcheck's round-by-round knowledge soundness
(G2) names ``\code{Interaction/Soundness.lean}'' (\code{bp:598-599}).

What exists at the new pin and could be consumed at the pin bump, through an adaptor:
\begin{itemize}
\item the one-polynomial sumcheck with \textbf{plain} soundness \code{count·deg/|F|} for every
  native prover (\lean{Native.execute_soundness}, \lean{Computable.execute_soundness}) and
  perfect completeness with a computable honest prover
  (\lean{Computable.execute_perfectCompleteness}), on any finite domain and for any individual
  degree bound. The blueprint's \lean{sumcheck_perfectCompleteness} for a summand that \emph{is}
  one polynomial is covered; its per-round \emph{knowledge} bound is not (item (f));
\item the honest round polynomial as a definition
  (\lean{Spec.SingleRound.projectedRoundPolynomial},
  \lean{Impl.Computable.projectedRoundPolynomial}/\lean{projectedMessage}) with proved degree
  bounds and the sum identity --- what leanerVM's staged pull request \#42 (``connect honest
  sumcheck polynomials to ArkLib'', \file{HonestSumcheckUpstream.lean}, now conflicting)
  re-derives against the old pin's \code{Spec} projection.
\end{itemize}

The adaptor a consumer would need (not written anywhere): a leanerVM \code{OracleReduction} whose
verifier \emph{is} a run of \lean{Native.Core.verifier} (or the computable one) with the
challenges read from the \code{ProtocolSpec} transcript, plus a lemma that the
\code{OracleReduction}'s acceptance coincides with the native \code{execute}'s non-rejection ---
a correspondence of the kind \#874 proves for one honest round
(\lean{legacy_honest_verifier_correspondence}) and \#1244 sketches (\lean{verifier_eq_unfolded}).
Even with it, the plain bound does not yield the spine's
\lean{rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWorstCaseWith} (\cref{sec:ark-composition}): the per-round leaf must
still be proved on the legacy side, or the typed framework must first define round-by-round
knowledge (its roadmap items 3--4).

\paragraph{(f) What remains leanerVM's.}
Nothing upstream, merged or open, covers leanVM's four sumcheck shapes; each is a local definition
with its own proof unless ArkLib's items 3--5 are done \emph{and} generalized:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{the virtual summand} (a formula of degree $d$ in $m$ oracle tables,
  \code{bp:880-884}): the typed sumcheck takes one polynomial oracle. Its \code{originalOracle} is
  a \lean{VirtualOracle}, so a formula over table oracles can be \emph{expressed} (the framework's
  substitution layer, \#869); but the theorem's \code{horiginal} requires that virtual oracle to
  be realized by one polynomial \code{p} of individual degree at most \code{deg}, and the final
  relation is \code{p(r) = target}, not ``the prover sends the table values at $r$ and the
  verifier evaluates the formula''. The last message and the \code{(Fin m → F)} output of
  \code{bp:889} are a further reduction, ours.
\item \textbf{the eq-weighted, back-loaded variant over tables of different heights}
  (\code{bp:898-902}; the gt-table-pub finding on \code{Seam.bus}, register row \emph{the bus
  seam admits statements} (\code{R2})): absent upstream; the structured sumcheck's
  $H = m \cdot t$ is the nearest shape but degree 2 only, without security theorems.
\item \textbf{the normalized (Gruen) round the GKR runs} (register row \emph{the GKR layer
  sumcheck is the normalized variant} (\code{R7}): ``Each deployed GKR round sends a degree-4
  cofactor \ldots{} the constant coefficient derived through the equality factor''): absent
  upstream; the typed verifier sums the sent polynomial over the domain, which is a different
  verifier.
\item \textbf{the round-polynomial encoding} (three of four coefficients sent, $c_1$ or $c_0$
  derived; obligation node 2.5.1.3.3): absent upstream; \#1128 gives only honest identities on
  the full polynomial.
\end{enumerate}

\paragraph{(g) Risks.}
\begin{itemize}
\item The classical leaf the ledger targets is \textbf{false as stated} at both pins (item (a))
  until \#1244 merges; a local proof ``contributed as the missing leaf'' would have to target the
  repaired statement, and the repair is on a framework upstream calls legacy
  (\cref{sec:ark-composition}).
\item ArkLib's declared direction is to prove round-by-round and knowledge notions on the
  \emph{typed} framework (``Repair or migrate legacy Sumcheck claims with correspondence and
  axiom checks; do not treat the native result as silently proving those old declarations'',
  \file{05-roadmap.md} item 5). A leanerVM proof on the legacy \code{Spec} may never be accepted
  upstream; a leanerVM proof on the typed framework cannot feed the spine's master theorems until
  that framework has knowledge soundness (\cref{sec:ark-typed}).
\end{itemize}

\section{Batching by the powers of one challenge}\label{sec:ark-batching}

\paragraph{(a)--(b) At both pins.}
Nothing. \code{git grep BatchingStrategy} at \code{7653a901} finds no declaration; the only
random linear combination in the library is inside the ring-switching batching phase
(\file{RingSwitching/Packing/BatchingPhase.lean}, the $\kappa$-coordinate batching vector of
[DP24], whose security theorem
\lean{RingSwitching.BatchingPhase.batchingOracleVerifier_rbrKnowledgeSoundness} is in the
baseline at both pins) and, as a component, \file{Component/SendChallenge.lean} (a verifier sends
\code{Fin ℓ → C}; it carries a \code{foldBlockStructure : CWSSStructure}, a coordinate-wise
special-soundness structure, and no round-by-round theorem).

\paragraph{(c) On \texttt{origin/main}.}
Nothing beyond the pin.

\paragraph{(d) Open pull requests.}
Pull request \#615 (feat(ring-switching): add reusable packing proofs and protocol integrations;
alexanderlhicks; open since 2026-07-07, last updated 2026-09-08, \code{mergeable: CONFLICTING},
\code{reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED}, 100 files, pre-module-system) carries the object the
blueprint's batching hole (G3) names, \lean{BatchingStrategy.gammaPowers}:
\src{\file{ArkLib/ProofSystem/RingSwitching/Packing/Batching.lean:88-91} at \code{ca7a2577} (the head of \#615)}
\begin{leancode}
structure BatchingStrategy (P : Type) [CommRing P] (W : Type) [Fintype W] where
  Challenge : Type
  [ftC : Fintype Challenge]
  [neC : Nonempty Challenge]
  weight : Challenge → W → P
  error : ℝ≥0
  separates : ∀ s s' : W → P, s ≠ s' →
    Pr_{ let c ←$ᵖ Challenge }[∑ u, weight c u * s u = ∑ u, weight c u * s' u] ≤
      (error : ℝ≥0∞)
\end{leancode}
\begin{leancode}
def gammaPowers (e : ℕ) : BatchingStrategy P (Fin e) where
  Challenge := P
  weight γ u := γ ^ (u : ℕ)
  error := ((e - 1 : ℕ) : ℝ≥0) / (Fintype.card P : ℝ≥0)
\end{leancode}
It is \textbf{not} an \code{OracleReduction}: it is a separation lemma (``distinct value
families coincide after weighting with probability at most \code{error}'') in the \code{Pr_{…}}
probability notation that ArkLib retired in \#913 (2026-09-21; \#615 predates that pull request
and the module system), with \lean{separates_map} (transport along an injective ring hom),
\lean{singleton} and \lean{reindex}. The pull request's own summary of its scope: ``Generic
pipelines use guarded composition with explicit extractors, knowledge states and per-prefix
bounds. Challenge errors sum to \code{batching error + m * (2/|C|)}.'' Closeness to merging:
\textbf{remote}. It conflicts with \code{main}, predates the module migration (\#897, the old
pin's own commit) and the probability migration (\#903, \#913), has no review, and its last
comment is the bot's timing report of 2026-09-08; issue \#893 (2026-09-29) lists it as a ``reuse
candidate'' whose ``Flock PCS/list/OOD integration and full FRI-Binius closure remain outside the
proved contracts''.

\paragraph{(e) What the blueprint plans locally that exists upstream.}
The batching hole (G3; \code{bp:600}: ``\code{batchClaims}, \code{(k − 1)/|F|}'', existing work
``\#43, ArkLib \#615's \code{gammaPowers}'') plans a \code{batchClaims : OracleReduction …} with
\lean{batchClaims_rbrKnowledgeSoundness} (\code{bp:907-911}). Nothing at the pin; \#615's
\lean{gammaPowers} is the scalar separation lemma only. leanerVM's staged pull request \#43
(``pair power-batched weight tables with columns'', mergeable, open since 2026-09-24) says of
itself: ``[ArkLib \#615] contains the scalar strategy but remains unavailable at leanerVM's
pinned revision. This contributes the table pairing and retains the necessary pinned scalar
compatibility; it does not establish batching knowledge soundness.''

\paragraph{(f) What remains leanerVM's.}
All of it: the separation lemma (a twenty-line Schwartz--Zippel on a univariate of degree
$< k$, which \lean{gammaPowers.separates} shows), the \code{OracleReduction} component with its
knowledge state function (``some claim is false'' before the challenge, ``the batched claim is
false'' after) and the worst-case round-by-round theorem. Under the inner-product interface of
register row \emph{the opening phase runs a sumcheck leanVM does not run} (\code{R18}), this
component \emph{is} the opening phase (gt-opening-compile A.5, alternative (ii)), so it is
load-bearing.

\paragraph{(g) Risks.}
Consuming \#615 for this would tie the opening phase to a hundred-file pull request that may
never merge, for a lemma of twenty lines. The repository's rule for its \code{To*} folders
(generic code goes to \file{ToArkLib/} and is offered upstream; recorded in the owner's memory
notes) fits: write it, offer it as its own small pull request, and cite \#615 for the idea.

A GKR written on the legacy composition inherits \code{sorryAx} unless composed with leanerVM's

\section{The oracle interfaces}\label{sec:ark-oracles}

\paragraph{(a)--(b) At both pins.}
\file{ArkLib/OracleReduction/OracleInterface.lean} (unchanged in content between the pins)
defines the class and these instances (line numbers at \code{7653a901}): \lean{instFunction} for
\code{α → β} (\code{:122}, a query is an argument), tensor and product interfaces
(\code{:142-191}), \lean{instPolynomial} (\code{:263}),
\code{instPolynomialDegreeLE : OracleInterface (R⦃≤ d⦄[X])} (\code{:270-273},
\code{Query := R}, answer \code{eval point}), \lean{instPolynomialDegreeLT} (\code{:277}),
\lean{instMvPolynomial} (\code{:283}, \code{noncomputable}, \code{Query := σ → R}),
\code{instMvPolynomialDegreeLE : OracleInterface (R⦃≤ d⦄[X σ])} (\code{:290-293},
\code{noncomputable}), \lean{instListVector}, \lean{instVector} (\code{:311}, \code{:317}, index
queries).

\textbf{Evaluation oracles for multilinears}: the Mathlib-side one is
\lean{instMvPolynomialDegreeLE} at \code{d = 1}, noncomputable. A \emph{computable} multilinear
evaluation interface exists once, local to Hachi:
\src{\file{ArkLib/Commitments/Functional/Hachi/Commitment.lean:67-72} (\code{7653a901})}
\begin{leancode}
instance multilinearEvalOracleInterface {n : ℕ} :
    OracleInterface (CMlPolynomial (Rq 𝓜(q, α)) n) where
  Query := Vector (Rq 𝓜(q, α)) n
  toOC :=
    { spec := Vector (Rq 𝓜(q, α)) n →ₒ Rq 𝓜(q, α)
      impl := fun p => do return CMlPolynomial.eval (← read) p }
\end{leancode}
over the cyclotomic ring \code{Rq}, not generic. leanerVM's \lean{evalOracle}
(\file{Field.lean:102-113} at \code{b435631}; obligation node 2.5.7.3) is the same shape over
\code{Column μ} with \code{eval₂Mle} into \code{E}.

\textbf{An inner-product (weighted-sum) oracle interface}: \textbf{none, anywhere upstream}
(\code{git grep -i} for \code{innerProduct}, \code{weightedSum}, \code{dotProduct … Oracle} at
\code{7653a901} across \file{OracleReduction}, \file{ProofSystem}, \file{Interaction},
\file{Data/MvPolynomial} finds no interface; the only hits are anonymous-constructor tuples in
proofs). The functional-commitment interface \lean{Commitment.Scheme}
(\file{Commitments/Functional/Basic.lean:59-79}) is generic over any
\code{OracleInterface Data}, so an inner-product interface instantiates it without change
(gt-opening-compile A.5, probe \file{InnerProductOracle.lean}, exit 0 at both pins per that
dossier).

\paragraph{(c)--(d) On \texttt{origin/main} and in open pull requests.}
Nothing. \#383 and \#615 add \code{OracleInterface} instances for their own message types only.

\paragraph{(e)--(f) What exists upstream, what remains ours.}
Upstream has the evaluation interface for Mathlib polynomials (noncomputable) and the generic
class; the inner-product interface the review recommends (register row \emph{the opening phase
runs a sumcheck leanVM does not run} (\code{R18}); obligation nodes 2.3.5.1, 2.5.7.3) is
leanerVM's to define, in Layer 0, with \code{Weight μ} as the query type and \lean{Weight.pair}
as the answer, and \lean{eqWeight_pair} making evaluation the special case
(\file{ClaimWeights.lean:51-54} at \code{b435631}). It is generic (``a weighted-sum oracle on a
table'') and belongs under \file{ToArkLib/} by the repository's rule, with a small upstream pull
request as the destination; nothing upstream plans it.

\paragraph{(g) Risk.}
None specific: the class is stable across the pins and the migration to the typed framework
keeps \code{OracleInterface} as the message-access primitive
(\file{Interaction/Oracle/Protocol.lean:58}
\code{oracleWith (Messages : Type u) (interface : OracleInterface.{u, u} Messages)}), so an
interface written today survives a framework change.

    (\file{ReedSolomon/MutualCorrelatedAgreement/Johnson/Probability.lean:41-52}, \#1198):
\src{\file{ArkLib/Data/CodingTheory/ReedSolomon/MutualCorrelatedAgreement/Johnson/Probability.lean:41-52} (\code{7653a901})}
\begin{leancode}
theorem mcaError_affineLine_johnson_le
    {F : Type} [Field F] [Fintype F] [SampleableType F] {n D : ℕ} {eta : ℝ}
    (domain : Fin n ↪ F) (hD : 1 ≤ D) (hDn : D ≤ n - 2) (heta : 0 < eta)
    (ha : johnsonAgreement n D eta ≤ 1) :
    mcaError (AffineLineGenerator F) (code domain (D + 1)) (1 - johnsonAgreement n D eta) ≤
      min 1 (ENNReal.ofReal
        (johnsonExceptionCount n D ⌈johnsonAgreement n D eta * n⌉₊ eta /
          (Fintype.card F : ℝ))) := by
\end{leancode}
    with \code{johnsonAgreement n D η = √(D/n) + η}
    (\file{HiddenDerivative/Parameters/Johnson/FiniteBounds.lean:70}) and
    \code{johnsonExceptionCount n D A η = (2μ−1)h + θ(h + μ + 4Dμh) + (n−D−1)μ}
    (\code{:104-108}, with $\mu$, $h$, $\theta$ the Johnson multiplicity, height and slack
    parameters of that file; ``the raw exception count of the characteristic-free
    ordinary-agreement argument'', closed upper bound \lean{johnsonExceptionCount_lt_closed}).
    The module docstring: ``\textbf{No characteristic hypothesis is needed.}'' Its weighted
    variant \lean{mcaError_affineLine_weightedJohnson_le} (\code{:72}) and the affine-space
    transfer \lean{mcaError_affineSpace_le_of_exactAgreement} (\file{LineToAffine.lean:173})
    exist. So at the new pin \textbf{a machine-checked Johnson-range MCA bound for affine lines
    over any finite field, binary included, is available}, with a different (and, by its own
    docstring, deliberately loose) constant from the printed BCHKS25 one that Annex B and the
    admitted theorem state. Whether its constant meets Annex B's per-level error budget at
    leanVM's parameters is \textbf{unverified} here (a numeric comparison of
    \code{johnsonExceptionCount} against BCHKS25's $a$ at $\rho \in \{1/2, \ldots, 1/16\}$,
    $n = 2^{\kappa+R}$ would settle it; gt-opening-compile F.2 has the scratch tool).
  \item \textbf{MCA up to capacity} (\#1208, \file{MutualCorrelatedAgreement/Capacity.lean}):
    \lean{capacity_lineAgreement} (\code{:131}), \lean{exists_capacity_mcaError} (\code{:254}),
    \lean{capacity_powerBatchingAgreement} (\code{:324}): exact correlated agreement at agreement
    $k + \delta n$ with gap-only constants $C n^{d+1}$. \textbf{Regime: every one of them carries
    the hypothesis \code{(ringChar F = 0 ∨ k - 1 < ringChar F)}}
    (\lean{HasCapacityLineAgreement}, \code{:118-121}; \lean{exists_capacity_mcaError},
    \code{:254-263}), which \textbf{fails for leanVM's binary fields} (\code{ringChar E = 2},
    $k - 1 \ge 2$ for any message length above three). The docstring says so: ``over any field
    of characteristic zero or larger than \code{k - 1}''; for lines at gaps $\delta \ge 6/25$
    the proof uses the first-order certificate, below it the rate-partition construction, both
    with the characteristic guard, and only ``when the curve characteristic guard fails, the
    line theorem uses the Johnson gap bound''. So the beyond-Johnson results do not apply to
    Annex B over $\E$; the Johnson-range theorem of item 2 does.
  \item List sizes: the pairwise Johnson list bound for arbitrary codes (\#910,
    \file{JohnsonBound/Pairwise.lean}, \file{ReedSolomon/ListDecodability/PairwiseJohnson.lean:50}
    \lean{code_isListDecodable_pairwiseJohnson}, \code{:75}, \code{:138}), proved --- Annex B's
    Johnson bound $L_i = 1/(2\eta_i\sqrt{\rho_i})$ (obligation node 2.1.2.4.2) has a proved
    upstream source, in the ``pairwise'' integral form $n(A-D)/(A^2-nD)$; the exact form used
    by Annex B is to be derived.
  \item Folding: \file{ProximityGap/Folding/{FoldingContext,ListDecodability,Multilinear}.lean}
    exist (\#825, \#845, per \#992's review notes: ``folding contexts and list-decoding
    preservation''); their fit with Annex B's Lemma B.10 ($2^{\ell-1}$ row union over the
    additive fold) is unverified here; \file{ProximityGenerator/BinaryTensorFoldAgreement.lean},
    \file{BinaryTensorFoldProbability.lean} (\#937, \#938: ``shared-level binary tensor fold'',
    ``tensor-fold probability'') are the closest names to WHIR's $k$-ary fold on binary fields.
  \item Interleaving: \file{ProximityGenerator/Interleaving.lean} (\#918 ``generalize
    interleaving MCA transfer'', \#932 ``exact agreement transfer for interleaved codes''); issue
    \#893 says ``ArkLib already provides the relevant interleaving error-transfer theorem; the
    exact list-transport and Flock extraction contracts remain work.''
  \item \lean{isMCAGenerator_of_isMDSGenerator} (\#902) proved ``in its unique-decoding range'';
    its all-radii form still admitted (\#992's note).
  \end{enumerate}
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{(c) On \texttt{origin/main}.}
Nothing beyond the pin.

\paragraph{(d) Open pull requests.}
\begin{itemize}
\item Pull request \#992 (feat(fri): prove end-to-end soundness of the computable IOP;
  alexanderlhicks; open since 2026-09-22, mergeable, no review, 40 files): ``Prove end-to-end
  ordinary and round-by-round soundness of the \textbf{actual computable FRI IOP specification}
  in \code{Fri.Spec.reduction}, against arbitrary adaptive provers: \code{Fri.Spec.soundness}
  \ldots{} \code{Fri.Spec.rbrSoundness} supplies the existing round-by-round security interface
  \ldots{} \code{Fri.Spec.reduction_run} proves the exact correspondence between the composed
  executable verifier and the bounded acceptance event''. ``The total error is the sum of
  ArkLib's existing powers-generator MCA errors plus \code{Real.toNNReal (1 - min θ δ) ^ l}.''
  It notes ``The general round-by-round-to-ordinary implication remains unfinished; this proof
  uses direct adaptive accumulation.'' Regime: FRI over \code{NonBinaryField} with smooth
  multiplicative cosets --- \textbf{not binary, not WHIR}. Fit: a \emph{pattern} for stating an
  IOPP's round-by-round soundness for a list relation on the legacy framework
  (\file{Security/Acceptance.lean}, \file{Accumulation.lean}, \file{BadEvents.lean} are new
  generic files), which is the shape Layer 11's \lean{whirOpen_rbrSoundness} needs. Closeness:
  forward-ported on 2026-09-22, no review since; \textbf{unknown}.
\item Pull request \#383 (feat: completeness and rbrKnowledgeSoundness of FRI-Binius protocols;
  chung-thai-nguyen; open since 2026-03-03, updated 2026-09-26, changes requested, conflicting,
  76 files): ``Completeness \& rbrKnowledgeSoundness for all FRI-Binius protocols: Binary
  Basefold, Ring-switching, FRI-Binius, simple ring-switching construction (BBFSmallFieldIOPCS)
  \ldots{} All PR-owned files are sorry-free; the top-level composed results inherit sorryAx from
  OracleReduction's composition layer.'' The author's last update (2026-09-24): ``DP24's
  ring-switching and FRI-Binius require laws beyond those in the default ring-switching profile,
  so we use a CoordinateLaws precondition for now.'' A maintainer comment (2026-09-08) says \#887
  already migrated the FRIBinius/BinaryBasefold \emph{completeness} on \code{main}. Fit with
  leanVM: Basefold over binary RS codes with the additive NTT is the closest upstream object to
  Annex B's WHIR (same code, 2-ary fold, no out-of-domain samples, no $k$-ary fold, no grinding,
  no weighted claims); its security proofs would rest on the legacy composition and on
  \lean{rs_mcaError_le_in_johnson_range}. Closeness: seven months open, second round of changes
  requested, conflicting; \textbf{remote}.
\item Pull requests \#776 (threshold-form public faces for the proved bound catalog), \#787
  (BCIKS20 separability repairs), \#792 (Grand List-Decoding witness constructors): coding-theory
  polish, none load-bearing for Annex B.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{(e) What the blueprint plans to consume that changed.}
The ledger row on mutual correlated agreement up to Johnson (A8, \code{bp:265}: ``Interface
\code{McaJohnson}, witness obligation [BCHKS25] Theorem 4.6 in ArkLib'') and the status
(\code{status:181}: ``ArkLib's coding-theory track (the \#907 slices landing on \code{main})''):
the \#907 port is \textbf{complete}, and it did \textbf{not} prove
\lean{rs_mcaError_le_in_johnson_range}; it proved a \emph{different} Johnson-range affine-line
bound (item 2 of (b)) that Annex B could cite instead, with its own constant. The blueprint's
\lean{McaJohnson} structure should be stated so that either theorem inhabits it (a bound
\code{mcaError (AffineLineGenerator E) (code domain k) δ ≤ a/|E|} with \code{a} a parameter), and
Annex B's error table re-derived for the proved constant if that is the one consumed
(\cref{f:ark-mca-stale}).

\paragraph{(f) What remains leanerVM's.}
WHIR itself (Annex B, Protocol B.1, Theorem B.7 with its per-level table; the $k$-ary fold on
the additive domain over $\K$ at level 0 and $\E$ after; out-of-domain samples; the weighted
claims; grinding as a message), the Merkle/BLAKE2s side, the parameters ladder, and the
list-binding compilation. The coding-theory inputs it needs beyond the line MCA bound (folding
preserves lists with the row union, out-of-domain separation, the Johnson list size in Annex B's
form) exist upstream as building blocks in some form (items 4--6 of (b)) and must be instantiated
and checked against Annex B; nothing upstream states them for WHIR.

\paragraph{(g) Risks.}
Annex B's Theorem B.7 is not machine-checked anywhere, and the two nearest upstream IOPP
soundness proofs (\#992 for multiplicative FRI, \#383 for binary Basefold) are open and
conflicting on the legacy framework. The capacity-range theorems that made the news are
inapplicable in characteristic two.

\paragraph{(a) At the old pin \texttt{dca90385}.}
\file{ProofSystem/RingSwitching/} (15 files): the family umbrella \file{Basic.lean} (``a family
of constructions, not one protocol'': \textbf{Packing}, small ring $\to$ large ring by a basis of
rank $2^\kappa$, [DP24] Construction 3.1; \textbf{Lift}, quotient ring $\to$ field, [HMZ25]),
\file{Transport/{Eval,Coeffs}.lean}, \file{RoundVerifiers.lean},

free of rank \code{2^κ} over \code{B}, a carrier \code{A}, two ring homs

\paragraph{(e) What the blueprint plans to consume.}

\paragraph{(f) What remains leanerVM's (or Flock's, leanerVM issue \#3).}
The $\mathrm{GF}(2) \to \K$ profile instance, the Annex A protocol as a \code{Phase.Def} at the

\paragraph{(g) Risks.}
Both open pull requests are long-lived, conflicting and unreviewed for weeks; the merged repair

% ====================================================================== section 10
\section{The typed \texttt{Interaction} framework's security notions, and the cost of migrating the spine}\label{sec:ark-typed}

\paragraph{(a)--(b) What the framework proves at the new pin (nothing of it at the old pin).}
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{Plain composition soundness} (\file{Interaction/CompositionSoundness.lean}, \#1218,
  \#1231): \lean{run_appendFlat_soundness} (\code{:227}), \code{_fixed} (\code{:210}),
  \code{_of_support} (\code{:191}), \code{_ae} (\code{:171}), \code{_weighted_ae} (\code{:122}),
  \code{_of_admissible} (\code{:260}): for a prefix truth-transition bound $\varepsilon_1$ and a
  suffix bound $\varepsilon_2$ (and an admissibility error $\delta$), the appended interaction's
  success is at most $\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2$ ($\varepsilon_1 + \delta + \varepsilon_2$),
  for every native prover, under lawful distribution semantics; the
  reachable/almost-everywhere/weighted forms allow branch-dependent suffix errors.
\item \textbf{Oracle composition}
  (\file{Interaction/Oracle/{Sequential,SourceRouting,CompositionSoundness}.lean}, \#1233,
  \#1234, \#1235): \lean{executeStrategies_append},
  \lean{executeStrategies_appendExported_close},
  \lean{executeStrategies_appendExported_soundness_ae} (\code{:302}), \code{_weighted_ae}
  (\code{:208}): a suffix reduction written against an \emph{exported} oracle interface composes
  with the prefix that exports it; the uniform bound is
  \code{εtruth + εinvalid + εsuffix}.
\item \textbf{Persistent runtime} (\file{Oracle/RuntimeSoundness.lean}, \#1237) and
  \textbf{access/cost certificates} (\file{Data/OracleComp/QueryBounds.lean}, \#1238).
\item \textbf{Security vocabulary}: soundness only.
  \code{git grep -i 'knowledge|extract|rbr|roundbyround'} over \file{ArkLib/Interaction} and
  \file{ArkLib/ProofSystem/Sumcheck/Interaction} at \code{7653a901} finds two docstring uses of
  ``extracted'' (a handler, a source behavior) and nothing else. There is no
  \code{KnowledgeStateFunction}, no extractor type, no round-by-round notion, no
  state-restoration notion, no Fiat--Shamir on this framework. The design chapter
  \file{03-adversarial-oracle-execution.md} §5--7 describes them as \emph{targets}: ``State
  restoration is a separate proposed security layer''; ``Knowledge soundness requires witness
  availability, not only a bound on true output claims. An offline extractor of a final
  execution path may learn a middle witness too late to supply it to the second protocol.
  Terminal offline knowledge soundness therefore does not compose in general''; ``The planned
  constrained execution tree \ldots{} Round-by-round state is indexed by full concrete
  prefixes''; ``These are target interfaces and dependencies, not consequences of the ordinary
  composition theorem.''
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{(c)--(d) Beyond the pin and in open pull requests.}
Nothing on \code{origin/main}; the only open pull request on the framework is the dependency
repin, pull request \#1251 (draft, dtumad, 2026-09-29: ``Repins VCVio to
Verified-zkEVM/VCVio\#821 \ldots{} moves VCVio's probability semantics onto Mathlib measures and
removes the discrete layer''; 59 files, all mechanical \code{Pr{x ← e}} $\to$
\code{Pr{let x ← e}} rewrites). When it merges, every probability statement in leanerVM's
bridges (\file{ToArkLib/GuardedVerdict.lean}, \file{ToVCVio/UniformSample.lean}) changes
notation again.

\paragraph{(e)--(f) What the blueprint could consume; what migrating would cost.}
Today nothing: the master theorems are \lean{rbrKnowledgeSoundnessWorstCaseWith} statements, a
notion the typed framework does not have. Migrating the spine would mean:
\begin{enumerate}
\item re-expressing every phase as a \lean{Verifier.Strategy}/\lean{Prover.Strategy} on an
  \lean{Interaction.Oracle.Protocol} tree (the commit phase as
  \code{.oracleWith (Column μ) evalOracle …}, the challenges as \code{.public .receiver E}), and
  the relations as predicates on \lean{ClosedClaim}s (statement plus observable oracle answers
  --- for the stack, the $2^\mu$ evaluations the relation reads, or the weighted sums under the
  inner-product interface);
\item waiting for, or writing, the round-by-round knowledge notion and its composition on that
  framework (roadmap items 3--4, no pull request), including the ``prefix-available witness
  extraction'' the design chapter says composition needs --- for the spine this is the commit
  phase's extractor, which reads the stack off the first message and is available to every
  suffix, so the spine is the easy case the design describes;
\item re-proving the two built phases and the port's role (the knowledge append) in the new
  vocabulary, and re-running every probe.
\end{enumerate}
The gain would be the removal of the local port and of the dependence on a framework upstream
calls legacy; the cost is that none of the target notions exists, and that the migration would
have to be redone if the framework's security definitions change while they are being written
(their design is explicitly ``fluid internals'' behind ``normative interfaces'',
\file{04-oracle-elimination-compiler.md:3}).

\paragraph{(g) Risk.}
The typed framework is where all upstream investment goes (the 2026-09-26 train
\#1214--\#1243 is its work), and the legacy framework's remaining admits are being
\emph{characterized as false} (\#1245) rather than proved. A spine that stays legacy must own
its composition theorems (it does) and must not plan on upstream repairs of
\file{Append/Security.lean}.

% ====================================================================== section 11
\section{The revised upstream ledger}\label{sec:ark-ledger}

One row per item of the blueprint's ledger (\code{bp:255-267}) and holes table
(\code{bp:594-617}) that names generic work, with two rows for items the ledger lacks.
``At the new pin'' is the declaration and its proof status at \code{7653a901}; ``in an open pull
request'' its number and state on 2026-09-30; ``proposed action'' is the proposal; the last
column lists the register rows (\cref{sec:reg}) and obligation nodes (\cref{sec:obl-tree}) the
item touches. Statuses: \emph{proved} = not in the axiom baseline; \emph{admitted} = in it. In
the first column the blueprint's ledger rows (A1--A9) and holes (G1--G6, C1, L1, K1--K3, P6, I1)
are named in words, with their codes in parentheses.

The register rows cited in the table, by name:
\begin{itemize}
\item \code{R2}: the bus seam admits statements the deployed table sumcheck cannot serve;
\item \code{R7}: the GKR layer sumcheck is the normalized variant; the blueprint gives it the
  wrong degree, the wrong error and no definition;
\item \code{R9}: one combiner more than GKR layers: the last is drawn and never used;
\item \code{R10}: Layer 5's generic GKR cannot be appended in the bus phase and cannot carry the
  zerocheck clause;
\item \code{R18}: the opening phase runs a sumcheck leanVM does not run;
\item \code{R19}: Layer 11's \code{whirOpen} batches a second time, and its \code{encode} serves
  level 0 only;
\item \code{R20}: no ArkLib theorem can inhabit the planned Fiat--Shamir and BCS interfaces, and
  the interface as commented is false;
\item \code{R21}: \code{verify_iff_compiled} names definitions that do not describe the compiled
  verifier;
\item \code{R22}: upstream Fiat--Shamir and BCS theorems will be about other constructions than
  leanVM's one-map BLAKE2s chain;
\item \code{R23}: the non-interactive error omits grinding, the list-size factor and the hash
  term, so it cannot carry leanVM's 128-bit claim;
\item \code{R24}: the list-binding compilation is a theorem the blueprint names and does not
  state;
\item \code{R25}: the proof of work is the one verifier check no planned theorem or mutation
  makes load-bearing;
\item \code{R26}: perfect completeness does not survive the Fiat--Shamir transform: the honest
  prover's grinding is a search;
\item \code{R34}: the blueprint plans on a framework ArkLib calls legacy, and on a pull request
  that may not merge;
\item \code{R138}: the compilation needs every phase before the opening to make no oracle query,
  and nothing states or enforces it.
\end{itemize}

% ====================================================================== section 12
\section{Findings}\label{sec:ark-findings}

Eight findings, in the survey's order. In quotations of the blueprint and the status and in the
proposed texts, as in those documents, a bare pull-request or issue number is leanerVM's and
ArkLib's are marked ``ArkLib''; elsewhere a bare number is ArkLib's.

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- 12.1
\begin{finding}{major}{f:ark-sumcheck-leaf-false}{The classical sumcheck leaf the ledger targets is false as stated at both pins}
\fhead{Classification} An error of the blueprint's plan (it names a false statement as the leaf
to prove) caused by an upstream defect; a deviation forced by an upstream library once \#1244 is
the reference.

\fhead{Evidence} \lean{Sumcheck.Spec.SingleRound.Simple.verifier}
(\file{Spec/SingleRound.lean:391-397} at \code{dca90385} and \code{7653a901}, quoted in
\cref{sec:ark-sumcheck}) sets the next target to \code{(oStmt ()).val.eval chal}, the input
polynomial's value; \lean{Simple.oracleVerifier} (\code{:423-436}) queries
\code{[OStmtIn R deg]ₒ} for it; the round-$i$ verifier (\code{:800}) is that verifier under
\code{liftContext} (\#1244's \lean{verifier_eq_unfolded}). ArkLib issue \#1, comment of
2026-09-27: the $\F_5$ counterexample, ``the input relation is false and the sum check passes''.
The admitted \lean{Simple.verifier_rbrKnowledgeSoundness} (\code{:570-573}) claims error
\code{deg/|R|} per challenge; at \code{deg = 0} the transition from a false input to an accepted
true output has probability one (paper: \code{outputRelation} is
\code{(oStmt ()).1.eval chal = newTarget}, \code{:354}, satisfied by construction). Pull request
\#1244 (open) repairs the statement.

\fhead{Proposed change}
\begin{change}{the ledger row on the sumcheck's round-by-round knowledge soundness (A1, \code{bp:258})}
\asis ``Layer 4 proves the single-round bound for its own sumcheck shape and contributes it as
the missing leaf.''
\asproposed ``Layer 4 proves the single-round knowledge bound for each of its own sumcheck
shapes, on the spine's notion. ArkLib's classical leaf
\code{Sumcheck.Spec.SingleRound.Simple.verifier_rbrKnowledgeSoundness} is admitted and, until
ArkLib \#1244 merges, false as stated (the verifier reads the input polynomial for its next
target); the typed sumcheck of \code{Sumcheck/Interaction/} proves plain soundness with no
knowledge notion. Nothing is contributed upstream until ArkLib has a knowledge notion for the
sumcheck.''
\reason The two upstream objects the row could mean are respectively false and of the wrong
kind.
\end{change}
\end{finding}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- 12.2
\begin{finding}{major}{f:ark-sumcheck-holes-sources}{The holes for the virtual sumcheck and for its round-by-round knowledge soundness name upstream sources that do not supply what they are listed for}
\fhead{Classification} Stale text of the blueprint and status (an error of the plan).

\fhead{Evidence} The ``Existing work'' of the hole for the virtual sumcheck (G1, \code{bp:598}):
``\#42, ArkLib \#1128, ArkLib \code{main}'s \code{Sumcheck/Interaction/}''; of the hole for the
sumcheck's round-by-round knowledge soundness (G2, \code{bp:599}): ``ArkLib \#1129,
\code{Interaction/Soundness.lean}''; status \code{status:198}: ``\#42's
\code{HonestSumcheckUpstream.lean} \ldots{} merged and the pin bumped; the adapter is deleted
then''. At \code{7653a901}: \file{Sumcheck/Interaction/Soundness.lean} proves one-round
\emph{plain} soundness of a committed message (\lean{executeCommitted_soundness}, \code{:131};
\lean{executeRandomCommitment_soundness}, \code{:167}) on the typed framework; the full
protocol's \lean{Native.execute_soundness} is plain soundness with \code{Unit} witness
(\cref{sec:ark-sumcheck}, item (b)); \#1128 is honest algebra; \#1129 is tests. None is an
\code{OracleReduction}, none is round-by-round, none has an extractor, none has a virtual
summand. leanerVM \#42 is now conflicting and targets the classical \code{Spec} projection,
whose verifier has the defect of \cref{f:ark-sumcheck-leaf-false}.

\fhead{Proposed change}
\begin{change}{the ``Existing work'' cells of the holes for the virtual sumcheck (G1) and for its round-by-round knowledge soundness (G2) (\code{bp:598-599})}
\asis G1: ``\#42, ArkLib \#1128, ArkLib \code{main}'s \code{Sumcheck/Interaction/}''; G2:
``ArkLib \#1129, \code{Interaction/Soundness.lean}''.
\asproposed G1: ``ArkLib \code{7653a901}: \code{Sumcheck.Interaction.Native} and
\code{Computable} (one-polynomial sumcheck on the typed framework, computable honest prover
\code{Impl.Computable.projectedMessage}, perfect completeness; consumable for the plain case
through an \code{OracleReduction} adaptor); \#42 for the honest algebra of the leanVM
variants''; G2: ``nothing upstream: \code{Native.execute_soundness} is plain soundness with no
extractor; ArkLib roadmap items 3--4 (native round-by-round and knowledge) have no pull request
(2026-09-30)''.
\reason A reader of the holes table would otherwise start the round-by-round hole (G2) by
porting a theorem of the wrong kind.
\end{change}
\end{finding}

% ---------------------------------------------------------------- 12.3
\begin{finding}{major}{f:ark-mca-stale}{The ledger row on mutual correlated agreement up to Johnson and the status's coding-theory row are stale in both directions}
\fhead{Classification} An error of the blueprint (it plans to consume a theorem whose proof is
not coming, and misses the one that exists); the constant mismatch with Annex B is a deviation
forced by the upstream library until compared.

\fhead{Evidence} \code{bp:265}: ``\code{rs_mcaError_le_in_johnson_range} is an external admit
\ldots{} witness obligation [BCHKS25] Theorem 4.6 in ArkLib''; \code{status:181}: ``ArkLib's
coding-theory track (the \#907 slices landing on \code{main})''. At \code{7653a901}: \#907 is
closed as complete (2026-09-26) and \lean{rs_mcaError_le_in_johnson_range} is still admitted
(baseline; \file{CapacityBounds.lean:203}), so the watched track will not prove it; but
\lean{ReedSolomon.mcaError_affineLine_johnson_le} (\file{Johnson/Probability.lean:41-52}, quoted
in \cref{sec:ark-whir}) is a \emph{proved} Johnson-range affine-line MCA bound over any finite
field with the constant \code{johnsonExceptionCount}; and the capacity-range theorems
(\file{Capacity.lean:118-121, 254-263}) carry \code{ringChar F = 0 ∨ k - 1 < ringChar F}, false
over $\E$.

\fhead{Proposed change}
\begin{change}{the ledger row on mutual correlated agreement up to Johnson (A8, \code{bp:265})}
\asis ``Interface \code{McaJohnson}, witness obligation [BCHKS25] Theorem 4.6 in ArkLib.''
\asproposed ``Interface \code{McaJohnson}, a bound
\code{mcaError (AffineLineGenerator E) (code domain k) δ ≤ a/|E|} with \code{a} a parameter.
Two inhabitants: ArkLib's admitted \code{rs_mcaError_le_in_johnson_range} (the printed [BCHKS25]
constant Annex B uses) and ArkLib's proved \code{ReedSolomon.mcaError_affineLine_johnson_le}
(\code{7653a901}, the [DKT26] constant \code{johnsonExceptionCount}, any characteristic); Layer
11 uses the proved one if its constant meets Annex B's per-level budget at the pinned parameters
(to be computed), else names the admitted one as the obligation. The capacity-range theorems of
the same port exclude characteristic two and are not usable.''
\reason Consume what is proved; say what is not.
\end{change}
\end{finding}

\fhead{Severity} Minor; it reinforces register row \emph{the blueprint plans on a framework

\section{Negative results and what was not verified}\label{sec:ark-negative}

\subsection{Checked and found as the blueprint says}

No finding on these:
\begin{itemize}
\item The ledger rows on knowledge-soundness composition (A2), context lifting (A4), Fiat--Shamir
  and BCS (A5) --- the admits ---, on WHIR, Merkle and BLAKE2s (A7: ``absent, only coding-theory
  lemmas'', for WHIR) and on the ring-switching packing leaves (A9: leaves admitted): confirmed
  at both pins by the baselines and by reading the files.
